headword: {三色団子|さんしょくだんご}

definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese sweet consisting of three rice dumplings on a skewer, each a different color: pink (or red), white, and green. Strongly associated with cherry blossom viewing (hanami) and spring.

examples.japanese: ⟦{花見|はなみ}→花見：01700_hanami⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{三色団子|さんしょくだんご}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{欠|か}かせない→欠かす：10138_kakasu⟧。
examples.english: Three-colored dango are essential for cherry blossom viewing.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもたち⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{三色団子|さんしょくだんご}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{嬉|うれ}しそう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{食|た}べていた→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: The children were happily eating three-colored dango.

examples.japanese: ⟦{春|はる}→春：00627_haru⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、{和菓子屋|わがしや}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{店先|みせさき}→店先：20728_misesaki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{三色団子|さんしょくだんご}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{並|なら}び→並ぶ：00605_narabu⟧、⟦{桜|さくら}→桜：02212_sakura⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{季節|きせつ}→季節：01304_kisetsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{訪|おとず}れ→訪れ：14267_otozure⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{感|かん}じさせて→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧⟦くれる→くれる：00724_kureru⟧。
examples.english: When spring arrives, three-colored dango line the shelves of Japanese sweet shops, reminding us that cherry blossom season has come.

notes:
Also called {花見団子|はなみだんご}. The three colors traditionally represent the seasons of spring: pink (⟦{桜|さくら}→桜：02212_sakura⟧, cherry blossoms), white (⟦{雪|ゆき}→雪：00584_yuki⟧, the last snow of winter), and green ({蓬|よもぎ}, fresh mugwort sprouts). Some interpretations link the colors to the progression of cherry blossoms: pink buds, white full bloom, and green leaves after the petals fall.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {三色団子|さんしょくだんご}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧: to eat three-colored dango
- {三色団子|さんしょくだんご}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{作|つく}る→作る：00481_tsukuru⟧: to make three-colored dango
- ⟦{串|くし}→串：19339_kushi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{刺|さ}した→刺す：02111_sasu⟧{三色団子|さんしょくだんご}: three-colored dango on a skewer

CULTURAL NOTE:
The saying ⟦{花|はな}より{団子|だんご}→花より団子：06213_hanayoridango⟧ (dango over flowers) humorously expresses the preference for practical pleasures like eating over aesthetic ones like viewing blossoms. {三色団子|さんしょくだんご} is one of the iconic treats behind this proverb. Available year-round at many shops, but peak season is March through April.
